haiku-low.q4: Users whose hash(salt + user_id) mod 10000 is below percent times 100, about 10% at 10 percent. Users who took the fallback are skipped.
haiku-low.q5: Stage must be shadow (or live_test in Path A), gate report passed and recent, ML lead approval for that exact version, and the feature check passing now.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED as decided. Product has not chosen; Path A adds an A/B test, Path B goes straight from shadow to 100%.
haiku-low.q7: Every instance polls the config store every 15 seconds and on startup. A revision change triggers download, hash check, feature check, smoke test, then atomic swap. No redeploy.

sonnet.q1: A popular-items list (first 20 of the cached list) with fallback: true. Lookup timeout/store error gives reason lookup_timeout; no record gives no_features (reason is logged, not returned). No retry.
sonnet.q2: The previous records stay in the online store and keep being served. Each record is judged by its own source_ts, and once it is older than 6 hours it counts as missing and the request falls back (stale_features). Alert after 2 failed runs, page at 4 hours.
sonnet.q3: No. Shadow output is only recorded, never shown to users. Shadow failures affect only shadow (fewer pairs, higher drop rate); the user's response and latency are unaffected because step 6 runs after the response is sent and never waits.
sonnet.q4: About 10% of users, chosen by hash(salt + user_id) mod 10000 < percent*100 (deterministic, so a user is always in or out; salt fixed while the candidate is in shadow). Only requests that did not take the fallback are copied, and only when a candidate is configured.
sonnet.q5: Stage must be shadow (or live_test in Path A); the shadow gate passed (at least 7 days of healthy shadow at 10%, error rate under 0.5%, p99 inference under 80 ms, skip/drop rates under ceilings, minimum pair count) with a recent report; ML lead approval recorded for that exact version; and the feature check passes at promotion time. Path A also requires the A/B stage to end in the candidate's favour.
sonnet.q6: Undecided. Product has not decided between a live A/B test (Path A) and going straight from shadow to 100% (Path B). The plan builds a select_version seam so either can be added.
sonnet.q7: Every instance polls the config store every 15 s and on startup; a changed revision number triggers a load. For a new active_version it downloads the artifact, checks the hash, re-runs the feature check, runs a smoke inference, then atomically swaps the in-memory snapshot. No redeploy needed. On failure it keeps serving the old version and retries on the next poll.
sonnet.q8: The shadow worker (separate deployment, same hardware class) looks up the candidate's own feature set itself and applies the same freshness/completeness rule using the candidate's required list. It adds no user latency because the hand-off happens after the response is flushed, via a bounded non-blocking queue on a separate service with no shared thread/connection pools, and nothing waits or retries on the request path.
sonnet.q9: If the queue is full or publish is slow/errors, the message is dropped and a counter incremented, with no waiting or retry. Messages over 60 s old at the worker are marked dropped_stale. Backlog shows up as fewer pairs and higher drop rate, and the drop counter appears in the gate report.
sonnet.q10: Pair records (request ID, user ID, both item lists, candidate latency, outcome, both source_ts) go to the shadow results table. An hourly comparison job computes overlap@20, rank correlation on shared items, popular-item share, catalogue coverage, and duplicate/unknown counts, aggregated by day and user segment into a report table read by a dashboard.
sonnet.q11: The registry feature check at registration: every required feature must exist in the online store schema and be actually materialized by at least one completed step 7 run; otherwise the stage is blocked_features and it cannot enter shadow or become active. The check is repeated at shadow start, instance load, promotion and rollback.
sonnet.q12: An on-call engineer triggers a rollback operation that runs the feature check on the target, then writes the rollback_target (or any previously active version) to active_version in the config store; no 7-day wait or approval; the bad version is marked retired. It is fast because instances poll every 15 s and the last two active versions stay loaded warm, so no download is needed.
